decisions.quote: The findings obtained support most of the original work, suggesting that machine translation can help language learners improve their EFL writing proficiency, specifically in strengthening lexical expressions.
decisions.reason: The abstract provides an overall affirmative verdict that the findings support most of the original work and confirm its main conclusion that machine translation improves EFL writing proficiency, without reporting any contrasting or failed finding.

parent_objection: Authors say findings obtained support most of the original work. Does this express a partial replication outcome (mixed), or genuine overall affirmative verdict successful under Rule1? The first reply demands explicitly named failed findings, but codebook also covers overall partial support. Distinguish support for usefulness of machine translation or broad main conclusion from empirical replication of original work as a whole. Do not invent which unmentioned findings failed or equate most automatically with either category; interpret exact source qualifier in context. If available source cannot settle empirical aggregate scope, explain uncertainty.
